t.4.43.1: Sugrīva, however, spoke of the matter especially to Hanumān, for he was certain that this best of monkeys would accomplish the purpose.
t.4.43.2: O bull among monkeys, I see no obstacle to your passage, neither on the earth nor in the mid-air, nor in the sky, nor in the abode of the gods, nor in the waters.
t.4.43.3: All the worlds, together with the asuras and the gandharvas, with the nāgas, men and deities, and with the oceans and mountains, are known to you.
t.4.43.4: O great monkey, O hero, your movement, speed, energy and nimbleness are equal to those of your father, the mighty Māruta.
t.4.43.5: In splendour, too, there is no being on earth equal to you; therefore bring about in very truth the means by which Sītā may be found.
t.4.43.6: In you alone, O Hanumān, are strength, intelligence and valor, and also statecraft attuned to place and time, O you who are learned in statecraft.
t.4.43.7: Then, perceiving that the fulfilment of the mission rested upon Hanumān, and knowing Hanumān well, Rāghava fell to reflecting.
t.4.43.8: This lord of the monkeys has placed his firm and settled hope in Hanumān in every way, and Hanumān is even more resolved upon accomplishing the task.
t.4.43.9: Therefore, for him who has thus set out, who is well known for his deeds and has been chosen by his master, the fruit of the task is certain to come.
t.4.43.11: Then the delighted scorcher of foes gave him a ring adorned with the mark of his own name, as a token of recognition for the king's daughter.
t.4.43.10: Beholding that monkey, eminent in resolve, the greatly splendid one became as though his purpose were already accomplished, his senses and mind filled with delight.
t.4.43.12: By this token, O best of monkeys, Janaka's daughter, free from alarm, looks upon you as one who has come from my presence.
t.4.43.13: Your resolve, O hero, your valor joined with strength, and the command of Sugrīva seem to announce success to me.
t.4.43.14: Taking it, that best of monkeys placed it upon his head and, with palms joined in reverence, bowed at his feet; then that foremost of leapers set forth.
t.4.43.15: Leading forth that mighty army of monkeys, the heroic monkey, son of the Wind-god, shone like the moon with its pure, unclouded orb in a sky from which the clouds have gone, graced by hosts of stars.
t.4.43.16: O you of immense strength, I rely upon your strength, O you whose valor is that of the foremost of monkeys; O son of the Wind, Hanumān, act with your abundant feats of valor so that Janaka's daughter may be reached.
